newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Brother seeks God's help for Pakistani CIA suspect.
newsitem.headline: Brother seeks God's help for Pakistani CIA suspect.

text.p: A half-brother of a Pakistani accused of killing two CIA workers said on Wednesday he was sorry for his relative's arrest by U.S. authorities and hoped God would protect the accused.
"He is our blood,... may God protect him," Hamidullah Kansi said. Mir Aimal Kansi's arrest was announced by the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) in Washington on Tuesday.
"We think he is innocent and we pray for his early release and return home," he told Reuters.
Hamidullah said he did not know how and where Aimal was arrested after being on the run for more than four years.
No comment was immediately available from Pakistani government authorities.
Aimal Kansi is accused of killing two CIA workers and wounding three others in a 1993 shooting spree outside the spy agency's headquarters at Langley, Virginia.
He is charged with murder, maiming and using a firearm in the commision of a crime. A judge in Fairfax, Virginia, on Wednesday ordered him to be held in jail without bail.
The FBI said Aimal Kansi, a Pakistani immigrant, had been delivered abroad by unidentified Afghan individuals to the custody of U.S. authorities, and then brought to Fairfax for trial.
FBI officials declined to give any further details about how Kansi was apprehended, or whether they would collect the $2 million reward that had been offered in the case.
The arrest of Kansi, scion of a well-known local tribe, evoked some sympathy for him in his home town of Quetta, capital of Pakistan's southwestern province of Baluchistan.
"He has been trapped, and if somebody had helped his arrest, it is shameful..., it is a mean act," said Quetta resident Mohammad Ismail.
"We don't think Aimal Kansi did this," said arms dealer Benaras Khan.
